occupation_label: agricultural scientist
description: Agricultural scientists research and study soil, animals and plants with the objective of improving agricultural processes, the quality of agricultural products or the impact of agricultural processes on the environment. They plan and implement projects such as development projects on behalf of clients or institutions.

occupation_label: aquaculture harvesting technician
description: Aquaculture harvesting technicians operate the harvesting process of aquatic organisms' production, managing the complex equipment and machinery used in the harvesting of specific cultured species.

occupation_label: zoo educator
description: Zoo educators teach visitors about the animals living at the zoo/aquarium as well as other species and habitats. They provide information about management of zoos, its collection of animals, and wildlife conservation. Zoo educators can be involved in both formal and informal learning opportunities ranging from production of information signs at enclosures to delivering classroom sessions linked to school or university curricula. Depending on the size of the organisation the education team may be a single person or a large team. Consequently the optional skills required are very broad and will vary from organisation to organisation. Zoo educators also promote conservation efforts. This can involve work within the zoo but also in the field as part of any zoo outreach project(s).

occupation_label: aquaculture hatchery manager
description: Aquaculture hatchery managers plan, direct, and coordinate the production in large-scale aquaculture operations to breed fish and shellfish, developing aquaculture breeding strategies using various types of spawning techniques. They control the reproduction and the early life cycle stages of cultured species. They supervise incubation, early feeding and rearing techniques of the cultured species.

occupation_label: performance video operator
description: Performance video operators control the (projected) images of a performance based on the artistic or creative concept, in interaction with the performers. Their work is influenced by and influences the results of other operators. Therefore, the operators work closely together with the designers, operators and performers. Performance video operators prepare media fragments, supervise the setup, steer the technical crew, program the equipment and operate the video system. Their work is based on plans, instructions and other documentation.

occupation_label: performance lighting designer
description: Performance lighting designers develop a lighting design concept for a performance and supervise the execution of it. Their work is based on research and artistic vision. Their design is influenced by and influences other designs and must be conform with these designs and the overall artistic vision. Therefore, the designers work closely with artistic directors, operators and the artistic team. During rehearsals and performance, they coach the operators to obtain optimal timing and manipulation. Performance lighting designers develop lighting plots, cue lists and other documentation to support the operators and production crew. They sometimes also work as autonomous artists, creating light art outside a performance context.

occupation_label: puppet designer
description: Puppet designers design and create puppets and manipulable objects for performers. Their work is based on research and artistic vision. Their design is influenced by and influences other designs and must be conform with these designs and the overall artistic vision. Therefore, the designers work closely with artistic directors, operators and the artistic team. Puppet designers make puppets and manipulable objects out of a variety of materials, and may build robotic elements into them. Puppet designers sometimes also work as autonomous artists, creating outside a performance context.

occupation_label: automated fly bar operator
description: Automated fly bar operators control the movements of sets and other elements in a performance based on the artistic or creative concept, in interaction with the performers. Their work is influenced by and influences the results of other operators. Therefore, the operators work closely together with the designers, operators and performers. Automated fly bar operators prepare and supervise the setup, program the equipment and operate automated fly bar systems, rigging systems or systems for horizontal movement. Their work is based on plans, instructions and calculations. The manipulation of heavy loads close to or above performers and audience makes this a high risk occupation.

occupation_label: sound operator
description: Sound operators control the sound of a performance based on the artistic or creative concept, in interaction with the performers. Their work is influenced by and influences the results of other operators. Therefore, the operators work closely together with the designers and performers. They prepare audio fragments, supervise the setup, steer the technical crew, program the equipment and operate the sound system. Their work is based on plans, instructions and other documentation.

occupation_label: product development manager
description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

**Essential Skills:**
*   **Case and Social Management:** Apply case management, plan social service process, organise social work packages, assess social service users' situation, review social service plan, apply decision making within social work, and apply problem solving in social service.
*   **Crisis and Support Intervention:** Apply crisis intervention, manage social crisis, provide social counselling, provide support to social services users, protect vulnerable social service users, contribute to protecting individuals from harm, and build helping relationship with social service users.
*   **Professional Standards and Ethics:** Meet standards of practice in social services, apply quality standards in social services, adhere to organisational guidelines, manage ethical issues within social services, accept own accountability, and undertake continuous professional development in social work.
*   **Social Work Practice:** Social work theory, clinical social work, apply person-centred care, apply holistic approach within social services, promote social change, empower social service users, advocate for social service users, and apply anti-oppressive practices.

Description we are looking for committed people who are interested in working with water and fishery care at the County Administrative Board I Jämtland County during the summer season 2025. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. Each service may include one or more of the following tasks:- Plan and lead the work on restoring watercourses, which is done together with excavator drivers in a team. - Action inventory of fleet -cleaned watercourses with the support of Esris applications Survey and Field Maps. - Manual restoration of streams. - Manually construct play areas for fish in watercourses. - Dust extracts. - Inventory and restoration of ditched wetlands. - Electric test fishing, web test fishing, cancer test fishing in lakes and streams. - Hiking obstacle inventory of older ponds and road crossings. - Conduct chainsaw and clearing work. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. If you share our passion to promote and preserve the biodiversity in our aquatic environments, we look forward to your application. We are looking for about 15-20 people for the field operations linked to our long-term work with water and fisheries. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. A significant portion of the tasks are performed in a place other than the place of employment Östersund, which means that overnight stays elsewhere may be required, sometimes during a whole work week. turns.content: What skills are needed for this occupation?

Based on the information provided from the database for the occupation of **Crisis situation social worker**, the following skills are required:

**Essential Skills:**
*   **Case and Social Management:** Apply case management, plan social service process, organise social work packages, assess social service users' situation, review social service plan, apply decision making within social work, and apply problem solving in social service.
*   **Crisis and Support Intervention:** Apply crisis intervention, manage social crisis, provide social counselling, provide support to social services users, protect vulnerable social service users, contribute to protecting individuals from harm, and build helping relationship with social service users.
*   **Professional Standards and Ethics:** Meet standards of practice in social services, apply quality standards in social services, adhere to organisational guidelines, manage ethical issues within social services, accept own accountability, and undertake continuous professional development in social work.
*   **Social Work Practice:** Social work theory, clinical social work, apply person-centred care, apply holistic approach within social services, promote social change, empower social service users, advocate for social service users, and apply anti-oppressive practices.
*   **Communication and Interpersonal:** Conduct interview in social service, communicate with social service users, negotiate with social service users, listen actively, relate empathetically, and negotiate with social service stakeholders.
*   **Community and Context:** Work within communities, deliver social services in diverse cultural communities, work in a multicultural environment in health care, promote inclusion, and make legislation transparent for users of social services.
*   **Professional Conduct:** Develop professional identity in social work, demonstrate leadership in social service cases, communicate professionally with colleagues in other fields, cooperate at inter-professional level, develop professional network, and address problems critically.
*   **Administrative and General:** Maintain records of work with service users, report on social development, have computer literacy, tolerate stress, manage stress in the work place, apply organisational techniques, and follow health and safety precautions in social care practices.
*   **Legal and Rights:** Legal requirements in the social sector, promote service users' rights, and social justice.

**Optional Skills:**
*   Assess the development of youth
*   Support the positiveness of youths
*   Promote the safeguarding of young people
*   Adolescent psychological development
*   Support children's wellbeing

occupation: social services manager
description: Social services managers have the responsibility for strategic and operational leadership and management of staff teams and resources within and or across social services. They are responsible for the implementation of legislation and policies relating to, for example, decisions about vulnerable people. They promote social work and social care values and ethics, equality and diversity, and relevant codes guiding practice. They are responsible for liaising with other professionals in criminal justice, education and health. They can be responsible for contributing to local and national policy development.

occupation: academic support officer
description: Academic support officers provide assistance to students with learning problems and act as the main point of contact for these students. They make sure extra tuition and educational programmes are provided to under-represented students with academic or personal issues. They also organise several social activities throughout the academic year.

occupation: educational psychologist
description: Educational psychologists are psychologists employed by educational institutions to provide psychological and emotional support to students in need. They are specialised in the provision of direct support and interventions to students, conducting psychological testing and assessment, and consulting with families, teachers and other school-based student support professionals, such as school social workers and educational counsellors, about the students. They may also work with the school administration to improve practical support strategies in order to improve the students' well-being.

occupation: teacher of talented and gifted students
description: Teachers of talented and gifted students teach students who have strong skills in one or more areas. They monitor the students’ progress, suggest extra activities to stretch and stimulate their skills, introduce them to new topics and subjects, assign homework and grade papers and tests, and finally they provide emotional support when needed. Teachers working with talented and gifted students know how to foster their interest and make them comfortable with their intelligence.

occupation: secondary school teaching assistant
description: Secondary school teaching assistants provide various support services to secondary school teachers such as instructional and practical support. They help with the preparation of lesson materials needed in class and reinforce instructions with students in need of extra attention. They also perform basic clerical duties, monitor the students' learning progress and behaviour and supervise the students with and without the teacher present.

occupation: nanny
description: Nannies provide qualified care services to children on the premises of the employer. They organise play activities and entertain children with games and other cultural and educative activities according to their respective age, prepare meals, give them bathes, transport them from and to school and assist them with homework on a punctual basis.

occupation: educational counsellor
description: Educational counsellors provide practical and emotional support to students in a educational institution, either in small groups, classrooms, or individually. They function as an accessible school official whom students may contact for a wide variety of issues. Educational counsellors may provide advice on personal problems such as social integration and behavioural issues, and on school-related matters such as composing adequate curriculum schedules, discussing test scores, and informing students on further education options. They may work closely with a school social worker and/or school psychologist and make referrals to other support services if necessary.

occupation: early years teaching assistant
description: Early years teaching assistants support the early years teacher in an early years or nursery school. They assist in class instruction, in classroom supervision in absence of the head teacher, and in organising, developing and putting into practice of the daily schedule. Early years teaching assistants monitor and help students in group as well as individually, and tend to focus on the students in need of extra care and attention the early years teacher cannot provide.

occupation: primary school teaching assistant
description: Primary school teaching assistants provide instructional and practical support to primary school teachers. They reinforce instruction with students in need of extra attention and prepare the materials the teacher needs in class. They also perform clerical work, monitor the students' learning progress and behaviour and supervise the students with and without the head teacher present.

occupation: special educational needs assistant
description: Special educational needs assistants assist special education teachers in their classroom duties. They tend to the physical needs of students with a variety of disabilities and help out with tasks such as bathroom breaks, bus rides, eating and classroom switches. They also provide instructional support to students, teachers and parents and prepare lesson programmes. Special educational needs assistants supply support for students tailored to their specific needs, help out with challenging assignments and monitor students' progress and classroom behaviour.

occupation: special educational needs teacher
description: Special educational needs teachers work with and teach children, young people, and adults with an intellectual or physical disability. They use a range of specialised concepts, strategies and tools to optimise learners' communication, mobility, autonomy, and social integration. They select teaching methods and support resources to enable individual learners to maximise their potential for independent living.

occupation: rehabilitation support worker
description: Rehabilitation support workers provide counselling to individuals dealing with birth defects or with major consequences caused by diseases, accidents, and burnouts. They help them to cope with personal, social and vocational issues. They assess the personal needs of clients, develop rehabilitation plans, get involved in the training, and help people undergoing a rehabilitation plan with job placement.

occupation: legal guardian
description: Legal guardians legally assist and support minor children, mentally disabled persons or incapacitated older adults in their personal life. They can manage their property, help with daily financial administration and assist with the ward's medical or social needs.

occupation: child care worker
description: Child care workers provide care for children when the parents or family members are unavailable. They look after the children's basic needs and help or supervise them during play. Child care workers can work for preschools, daycare centres, childcare agencies or individual families.

occupation: adult community care worker
description: Adult community care workers perform assessment and care management of communities of adults who live with physical impairments or convalescing states. They aim to improve their life in the community and enable them to live safely and independently at their own home.

They assess the level of risk, mobilise client resources, and stabilise the crisis.']), Turn(role='user', content='What skills are essential?'), Turn(role='assistant', content="The essential skills for a crisis situation social worker, based on the provided data, are:

*   **Social Justice:** Applying the principles of human rights and social justice on a case-by-case basis.
*   **Apply anti-oppressive practices:** Identifying oppression and enabling service users to improve their lives and environment.
*   **Provide social counselling:** Assisting and guiding users to resolve personal, social, or psychological difficulties.
*   **Social work theory:** Understanding theories underpinned by social sciences and humanities.
*   **Involve service users and carers in care planning:** Evaluating care needs and involving families in support plans.
*   **Work within communities:** Establishing social projects for community development.
*   **Meet standards of practice in social services:** Practicing in a lawful, safe, and effective way.
*   **Empower social service users:** Enabling individuals and communities to gain control over their lives.
*   **Apply quality standards in social services:** Upholding social work values while applying quality standards.
*   **Apply case management:** Assessing, planning, coordinating, and advocating for services on behalf of a person.
*   **Apply problem solving in social service:** Using a systematic, step-by-step process to provide services.
*   **Apply crisis intervention:** Responding methodologically to disruptions in the normal functioning of a person, family, or community.
*   **Legal requirements in the social sector:** Understanding prescribed legislative and regulatory requirements.
*   **Protect vulnerable social service users:** Providing support in dangerous situations and removing users to safety.
*   **Contribute to protecting individuals from harm:** Reporting dangerous, abusive, or discriminatory behavior.
*   **Develop professional identity in social work:** Understanding the professional framework and the specific needs of clients.
*   **Provide support to social services users:** Helping users identify strengths and make informed decisions.
*   **Deliver social services in diverse cultural communities:** Being mindful of different cultural traditions and human rights policies.
*   **Social sciences:** Applying sociological, anthropological, and psychological theories.
*   **Conduct interview in social service:** Exploring a client's experiences, attitudes, and opinions.
*   **Demonstrate leadership in social service cases:** Taking the lead in the practical handling of cases.
*   **Communicate professionally with colleagues in other fields:** Cooperating with other professionals in health and social services.
*   **Follow health and safety precautions in social care practices:** Ensuring hygienic and safe environments.
*   **Plan social service process:** Defining objectives, identifying resources, and establishing evaluation indicators.
*   **Promote social change:** Taking into account unpredictable changes at micro, macro, and mezzo levels.
*   **Advocate for social service users:** Speaking on behalf of less advantaged users.
*   **Prevent social problems:** Implementing actions to enhance the quality of life for all citizens.
*   **Make legislation transparent for users of social services:** Explaining legislative implications to users.
*   **Negotiate with social service users:** Building trust and encouraging cooperation.
*   **Promote service users' rights:** Supporting a client's right to control their life and make informed choices.
*   **Apply person-centred care:** Putting individuals at the heart of all decisions.
*   **Clinical social work:** Assessing, diagnosing, and treating bio-psychological problems and behavioral disturbances.
*   **Assess social service users' situation:** Balancing curiosity and respect while identifying needs, resources, and risks.
*   **Crisis intervention:** Utilizing coping strategies to help individuals overcome problems and avoid psychological breakdown.
*   **Relate empathetically:** Recognizing and sharing the emotions and insights of others.
*   **Listen actively:** Giving full attention to others and providing solutions accordingly.
*   **Manage social crisis:** Responding to social crises in a timely manner using available resources.
*   **Manage ethical issues within social services:** Applying ethical principles to resolve dilemmas.
*   **Review social service plan:** Following up on plans while considering user feedback.
*   **Apply decision making within social work:** Making decisions within the limits of authority while considering user input.
*   **Adhere to organisational guidelines:** Understanding and following organizational standards and motives.
*   **Apply holistic approach within social services:** Recognizing connections between different dimensions of social problems and policies.
*   **Work in a multicultural environment in health care:** Interacting with individuals from various cultures.
*   **Address problems critically:** Identifying strengths and weaknesses in approaches to formulate solutions.
*   **Apply socially just working principles:** Working in accordance with human rights and organizational values.
*   **Promote inclusion:** Preventing discrimination and ensuring a positive environment.
*   **Maintain records of work with service users:** Keeping accurate and timely records while complying with privacy legislation.
*   **Develop professional network:** Reaching out to others in a professional context for mutual benefit.
*   **Negotiate with social service stakeholders:** Dealing with institutions, employers, and landlords to achieve the best result for the client.
*   **Report on social development:** Presenting results and conclusions in an intelligible way.
*   **Undertake continuous professional development in social work:** Updating knowledge and skills within one's scope of practice.
*   **Have computer literacy:** Utilizing modern IT equipment and technology.
*   **Tolerate stress:** Maintaining effective performance under pressure.
*   **Apply organisational techniques:** Employing procedures to facilitate goals and manage schedules.
*   **Refer social service users:** Making referrals to other professionals or organizations based on needs.
*   **Organise social work packages:** Creating support services according to regulations and timescales.
*   **Communicate with social service users:** Using various communication methods tailored to the user's needs and culture.
*   **Consider social impact of actions on service users:** Considering the political and cultural context of actions.
*   **Cooperate at inter-professional level:** Working with people in other sectors.
*   **Company policies:** Understanding the rules governing organizational activity.
*   **Accept own accountability:** Recognizing the limits of one's own scope of practice.

title: Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals
description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. title: Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals
description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. If you also have experience in project management and work with skills development, as well as experience in working with small business owners, this is advantageous. You have the ability to communicate clearly in both speech and writing and have an established network within the agricultural industry. You are structured and solution-oriented with good computer skills. The position involves travel, mainly in the county, but longer trips with overnight stays also occur. A driver's license for a passenger car is required. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference to our county and society. The County Board is a broad authority, which means that you constantly have the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a strong focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health-promoting wellness activities. We are keen on cooperation with our union partners and can offer remote work. In case of permanent employment at the County Board, you will be placed at war with the authority. Depending on the service, this may include serving in crisis staff and security classification. We usually start with trial employment for permanent positions. You can find information about how we process your personal data at www.lansstyrelsen.se/dataskydd

Descriptions The newly formed function of agricultural support we are now looking for a manager. The function consists of between 10 -15 Employees depending on the season and work mainly with handling and control of animal and area-based support for agriculture, register checks on animals and land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties. The function also participates in cross -sectoral collaborations on the county administrative board and acts as experts when answering referrals and when preparing various issues linked to the county's agriculture. Work tasks as a function manager will be your role to lead the work based on our assignment and in accordance with the county administrative board's overall priorities. In daily work, you are a present manager who practices a trust -based leadership to create a good workplace for your employees and colleagues. You have target and results responsibility for the function and work closely with the unit manager and deputy unit manager on issues related to financial follow-up and strategic planning. You are part of the unit's management team and together with other managers take overall responsibility for the unit's operations and development. Collaborations with other function managers on the county administrative board and in cross -sectoral working groups are a natural part of your work. In addition to your managerial assignment you will also work with other tasks that are included in the operation of the function or unit. Depending on your background and competence, the data may vary but will constitute approximately 50% of your working hours. Qualification you have college education in an area relevant to the service, for example as an agronomist or surveyor or other education that the employer considers equivalent. You have experience of personnel management and being manager and leader and are confident in that role. Furthermore, you have knowledge and experience of issues related to agriculture and food production and a good understanding of the conditions that apply to Swedish agriculture. If you have experience in support management or work at the authority, it is a merit. You are a responsive manager who is good at listening and who can create commitment to your employees. title: Säsongsarbetare till Vattenenheten
description: The County Administrative Board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to safeguard the qualities that diversity adds the business. At the water unit, more than 30 employees work. Here we work broadly with issues regarding water, fishing and environmental monitoring in the county. Everything from restoration of aquatic environments, liming and fishing to water management, environmental analysis and drinking water supply. The unit also runs its own water laboratory, which in turn is a central role in the county administrative boards' work with calke power follow -up. The water unit is constantly working to increase the pace of action and the action setting in the county partly by communicating contributions to local water conservation projects and fishing projects through fishing care grants, and partly by seeking new water conservation projects within the EU's various environmental and fisheries funds. At the unit, experts work who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness to the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! Description we are looking for committed people who are interested in working with water and fishery care at the County Administrative Board I Jämtland County during the summer season 2025. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. If you share our passion to promote and preserve the biodiversity in our aquatic environments, we look forward to your application. We are looking for about 15-20 people for the field operations linked to our long-term work with water and fisheries. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. A significant portion of the tasks are performed in a place other than the place of employment Östersund, which means that overnight stays elsewhere may be required, sometimes during a whole work week. The opportunities for holidays are limited. Work tasks have been primarily to participate in the field operations. Preparations, data settlement and compilations of field work performed can also be included. Other business -related tasks may also be relevant. Each service may include one or more of the following tasks:- Plan and lead the work on restoring watercourses, which is done together with excavator drivers in a team. - Action inventory of fleet -cleaned watercourses with the support of Esris applications Survey and Field Maps. - Manual restoration of streams. - Manually construct play areas for fish in watercourses. - Dust extracts. - Inventory and restoration of ditched wetlands. - Electric test fishing, web test fishing, cancer test fishing in lakes and streams. - Hiking obstacle inventory of older ponds and road crossings. - Conduct chainsaw and clearing work. Enter the date in the application when you can start and how long you can work. We value these properties highly. You must master the Swedish language in speech and writing. We strive for an equal working environment. To perform the work you need to have good field experience, be physically equipped to spend all days in forest and land, wade in running water, work from boat and carry field equipment to and from watercourses. The work includes trips within the county, which means that B-driving license is a requirement. Extra merit for the service is if you have science education with relevant focus and/or experience in field work in the areas included in the tasks, especially task 1, 2, 3 And 7.Andr merit qualifications include a strong interest in water conservation, fishing care and nature conservation. description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. If you also have experience in project management and work with skills development, as well as experience in working with small business owners, this is advantageous. You have the ability to communicate clearly in both speech and writing and have an established network within the agricultural industry. You are structured and solution-oriented with good computer skills. The position involves travel, mainly in the county, but longer trips with overnight stays also occur. A driver's license for a passenger car is required. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference to our county and society. The County Board is a broad authority, which means that you constantly have the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a strong focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health-promoting wellness activities. description: The County Administrative Board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to safeguard the qualities that diversity adds the business. At the water unit, more than 30 employees work. Here we work broadly with issues regarding water, fishing and environmental monitoring in the county. Everything from restoration of aquatic environments, liming and fishing to water management, environmental analysis and drinking water supply. The unit also runs its own water laboratory, which in turn is a central role in the county administrative boards' work with calke power follow -up. The water unit is constantly working to increase the pace of action and the action setting in the county partly by communicating contributions to local water conservation projects and fishing projects through fishing care grants, and partly by seeking new water conservation projects within the EU's various environmental and fisheries funds. At the unit, experts work who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness to the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! Description we are looking for committed people who are interested in working with water and fishery care at the County Administrative Board I Jämtland County during the summer season 2025. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. If you share our passion to promote and preserve the biodiversity in our aquatic environments, we look forward to your application. We are looking for about 15-20 people for the field operations linked to our long-term work with water and fisheries. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. A significant portion of the tasks are performed in a place other than the place of employment Östersund, which means that overnight stays elsewhere may be required, sometimes during a whole work week. The opportunities for holidays are limited. Work tasks have been primarily to participate in the field operations. Preparations, data settlement and compilations of field work performed can also be included. Other business -related tasks may also be relevant. Each service may include one or more of the following tasks:- Plan and lead the work on restoring watercourses, which is done together with excavator drivers in a team. - Action inventory of fleet -cleaned watercourses with the support of Esris applications Survey and Field Maps. - Manual restoration of streams. - Manually construct play areas for fish in watercourses. - Dust extracts. - Inventory and restoration of ditched wetlands. - Electric test fishing, web test fishing, cancer test fishing in lakes and streams. - Hiking obstacle inventory of older ponds and road crossings. - Conduct chainsaw and clearing work. Enter the date in the application when you can start and how long you can work. We value these properties highly. You must master the Swedish language in speech and writing. We strive for an equal working environment. To perform the work you need to have good field experience, be physically equipped to spend all days in forest and land, wade in running water, work from boat and carry field equipment to and from watercourses. The work includes trips within the county, which means that B-driving license is a requirement. Extra merit for the service is if you have science education with relevant focus and/or experience in field work in the areas included in the tasks, especially task 1, 2, 3 And 7.Andr merit qualifications include a strong interest in water conservation, fishing care and nature conservation. turns.content: Which occupation helps people during emergencies and difficult life situations?

Although there is no information in the database specifically addressing agricultural occupations related to this inquiry, the database provides information regarding a "crisis situation social worker."

A crisis situation social worker provides emergency support and assistance to persons with physical or mental disorders by addressing their distress, impairment, and instability. They are responsible for assessing the level of risk, mobilising client resources, and stabilising the crisis.

turns.content: What skills are essential?

The essential skills for a crisis situation social worker, based on the provided data, are:

*   **Social Justice:** Applying the principles of human rights and social justice on a case-by-case basis.
*   **Apply anti-oppressive practices:** Identifying oppression and enabling service users to improve their lives and environment.
*   **Provide social counselling:** Assisting and guiding users to resolve personal, social, or psychological difficulties.
*   **Social work theory:** Understanding theories underpinned by social sciences and humanities.
*   **Involve service users and carers in care planning:** Evaluating care needs and involving families in support plans.
*   **Work within communities:** Establishing social projects for community development.
*   **Meet standards of practice in social services:** Practicing in a lawful, safe, and effective way.
*   **Empower social service users:** Enabling individuals and communities to gain control over their lives.
*   **Apply quality standards in social services:** Upholding social work values while applying quality standards.
*   **Apply case management:** Assessing, planning, coordinating, and advocating for services on behalf of a person.
*   **Apply problem solving in social service:** Using a systematic, step-by-step process to provide services.
*   **Apply crisis intervention:** Responding methodologically to disruptions in the normal functioning of a person, family, or community.
*   **Legal requirements in the social sector:** Understanding prescribed legislative and regulatory requirements.
*   **Protect vulnerable social service users:** Providing support in dangerous situations and removing users to safety.
*   **Contribute to protecting individuals from harm:** Reporting dangerous, abusive, or discriminatory behavior.
*   **Develop professional identity in social work:** Understanding the professional framework and the specific needs of clients.
*   **Provide support to social services users:** Helping users identify strengths and make informed decisions.
*   **Deliver social services in diverse cultural communities:** Being mindful of different cultural traditions and human rights policies.
*   **Social sciences:** Applying sociological, anthropological, and psychological theories.
*   **Conduct interview in social service:** Exploring a client's experiences, attitudes, and opinions.
*   **Demonstrate leadership in social service cases:** Taking the lead in the practical handling of cases.
*   **Communicate professionally with colleagues in other fields:** Cooperating with other professionals in health and social services.
*   **Follow health and safety precautions in social care practices:** Ensuring hygienic and safe environments.
*   **Plan social service process:** Defining objectives, identifying resources, and establishing evaluation indicators.
*   **Promote social change:** Taking into account unpredictable changes at micro, macro, and mezzo levels.
*   **Advocate for social service users:** Speaking on behalf of less advantaged users.
*   **Prevent social problems:** Implementing actions to enhance the quality of life for all citizens.
*   **Make legislation transparent for users of social services:** Explaining legislative implications to users.
*   **Negotiate with social service users:** Building trust and encouraging cooperation.
*   **Promote service users' rights:** Supporting a client's right to control their life and make informed choices.
*   **Apply person-centred care:** Putting individuals at the heart of all decisions.
*   **Clinical social work:** Assessing, diagnosing, and treating bio-psychological problems and behavioral disturbances.
*   **Assess social service users' situation:** Balancing curiosity and respect while identifying needs, resources, and risks.
*   **Crisis intervention:** Utilizing coping strategies to help individuals overcome problems and avoid psychological breakdown.
*   **Relate empathetically:** Recognizing and sharing the emotions and insights of others.
*   **Listen actively:** Giving full attention to others and providing solutions accordingly.
*   **Manage social crisis:** Responding to social crises in a timely manner using available resources.
*   **Manage ethical issues within social services:** Applying ethical principles to resolve dilemmas.
*   **Review social service plan:** Following up on plans while considering user feedback.
*   **Apply decision making within social work:** Making decisions within the limits of authority while considering user input.
*   **Adhere to organisational guidelines:** Understanding and following organizational standards and motives.
*   **Apply holistic approach within social services:** Recognizing connections between different dimensions of social problems and policies.
*   **Work in a multicultural environment in health care:** Interacting with individuals from various cultures.
*   **Address problems critically:** Identifying strengths and weaknesses in approaches to formulate solutions.
*   **Apply socially just working principles:** Working in accordance with human rights and organizational values.
*   **Promote inclusion:** Preventing discrimination and ensuring a positive environment.
*   **Maintain records of work with service users:** Keeping accurate and timely records while complying with privacy legislation.
*   **Develop professional network:** Reaching out to others in a professional context for mutual benefit.
*   **Negotiate with social service stakeholders:** Dealing with institutions, employers, and landlords to achieve the best result for the client.
*   **Report on social development:** Presenting results and conclusions in an intelligible way.
*   **Undertake continuous professional development in social work:** Updating knowledge and skills within one's scope of practice.
*   **Have computer literacy:** Utilizing modern IT equipment and technology.
*   **Tolerate stress:** Maintaining effective performance under pressure.
*   **Apply organisational techniques:** Employing procedures to facilitate goals and manage schedules.
*   **Refer social service users:** Making referrals to other professionals or organizations based on needs.
*   **Organise social work packages:** Creating support services according to regulations and timescales.
*   **Communicate with social service users:** Using various communication methods tailored to the user's needs and culture.
*   **Consider social impact of actions on service users:** Considering the political and cultural context of actions.
*   **Cooperate at inter-professional level:** Working with people in other sectors.
*   **Company policies:** Understanding the rules governing organizational activity.
*   **Accept own accountability:** Recognizing the limits of one's own scope of practice.
*   **Manage stress in the work place:** Coping with professional and institutional stress to avoid burnout.
*   **Build helping relationship with social service users:** Fostering trust through authentic, empathetic, and caring interaction.

turns.content: Are there any open positions related to that occupation?

Based on the information provided in the database, there are no open positions listed for a "crisis situation social worker."

However, the database does contain information about currently open positions within the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County related to agricultural and rural administration. These include:

*   **Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals:** This role involves planning and implementing skills development for farmers (advice, courses, and farm meetings), coordinating actors, and handling project fund applications.
*   **Chef till funktionen Jordbrukarstöd (Manager for the Agricultural Support function):** A leadership position responsible for managing 10–15 employees who handle animal and area-based support, register checks on animals, and land acquisition permits.
*   **Säsongsarbetare till Vattenenheten (Seasonal workers for the Water Unit):** Positions focused on field operations for water and fishery conservation, such as restoring watercourses, manual restoration of streams, and inventory work. 

While these roles do not match the occupation of a social worker, some positions—specifically those at the County Administrative Board—note that the work may include "service in crisis staff" as part of the employment requirements.

title: Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals
description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to take advantage of the qualities that diversity brings to the business. The rural unit is one of the county board's seven units with approximately 40 employees. The unit is responsible for project and investment support, animal and area-based support, advice and courses for agricultural companies, supervision in agriculture, register checks on animals, land acquisition permits for agricultural and forestry properties and monitoring of basic paid services. Within the unit there is also the Interreg Sweden Norway program for which the County Administrative Board of Jämtland County is the managing authority. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. If you also have experience in project management and work with skills development, as well as experience in working with small business owners, this is advantageous. You have the ability to communicate clearly in both speech and writing and have an established network within the agricultural industry. You are structured and solution-oriented with good computer skills. The position involves travel, mainly in the county, but longer trips with overnight stays also occur. A driver's license for a passenger car is required. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference to our county and society. The County Board is a broad authority, which means that you constantly have the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a strong focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health-promoting wellness activities. We are keen on cooperation with our union partners and can offer remote work. In case of permanent employment at the County Board, you will be placed at war with the authority. Depending on the service, this may include serving in crisis staff and security classification. We usually start with trial employment for permanent positions. title: Säsongsarbetare till Vattenenheten
description: The County Administrative Board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. We work to be an authority free from discrimination and want to safeguard the qualities that diversity adds the business. At the water unit, more than 30 employees work. Here we work broadly with issues regarding water, fishing and environmental monitoring in the county. Everything from restoration of aquatic environments, liming and fishing to water management, environmental analysis and drinking water supply. The unit also runs its own water laboratory, which in turn is a central role in the county administrative boards' work with calke power follow -up. The water unit is constantly working to increase the pace of action and the action setting in the county partly by communicating contributions to local water conservation projects and fishing projects through fishing care grants, and partly by seeking new water conservation projects within the EU's various environmental and fisheries funds. At the unit, experts work who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness to the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! Description we are looking for committed people who are interested in working with water and fishery care at the County Administrative Board I Jämtland County during the summer season 2025. The work focuses on improving the habitats for fish, river pearl mussel, otters and other aquatic species in the county's water. If you share our passion to promote and preserve the biodiversity in our aquatic environments, we look forward to your application. We are looking for about 15-20 people for the field operations linked to our long-term work with water and fisheries. The work is largely done in ongoing restoration projects, such as the EU projects Rivers of Life and Ecostreams for Life but also in other assignments linked to water conservation and fishing. The services may vary in time from about 3-6 months. Most of the work takes place in the field between June and October. Some of the services may be relevant to start earlier and completed later and contain more administrative tasks. A significant portion of the tasks are performed in a place other than the place of employment Östersund, which means that overnight stays elsewhere may be required, sometimes during a whole work week. The opportunities for holidays are limited. Work tasks have been primarily to participate in the field operations. Preparations, data settlement and compilations of field work performed can also be included. Other business -related tasks may also be relevant. Each service may include one or more of the following tasks:- Plan and lead the work on restoring watercourses, which is done together with excavator drivers in a team. - Action inventory of fleet -cleaned watercourses with the support of Esris applications Survey and Field Maps. - Manual restoration of streams. - Manually construct play areas for fish in watercourses. - Dust extracts. - Inventory and restoration of ditched wetlands. - Electric test fishing, web test fishing, cancer test fishing in lakes and streams. - Hiking obstacle inventory of older ponds and road crossings. - Conduct chainsaw and clearing work. Enter the date in the application when you can start and how long you can work. We value these properties highly. You must master the Swedish language in speech and writing. We strive for an equal working environment. To perform the work you need to have good field experience, be physically equipped to spend all days in forest and land, wade in running water, work from boat and carry field equipment to and from watercourses. The work includes trips within the county, which means that B-driving license is a requirement. Extra merit for the service is if you have science education with relevant focus and/or experience in field work in the areas included in the tasks, especially task 1, 2, 3 And 7.Andr merit qualifications include a strong interest in water conservation, fishing care and nature conservation. We will process applications and initiate interviews on an ongoing basis.We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference for our county and society. The County Administrative Board is a broad authority, which means that you are constantly being given the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. j.id: 74028", "j.title: Agronomist
j.description: Agronomist - Frövi GreeneryWe are looking for an experienced and dedicated agronomist to join our cultivation department. In this role, you will have the opportunity to combine your expertise with innovation in greenhouse farming. Are you ready to take the next step in your career and contribute to a sustainable future? Then this is the job for you!About Frövi Greenery - Pioneers in the Greenhouse IndustryFoodVentures has launched its first project in the Nordics, Frövi Greenery, as part of its global expansion. Founded in 2012, FoodVentures has become a global leader in high-tech greenhouses, delivering fresh vegetables from modern farms to cities around the world. We manage the entire value chain, from seed to supermarket, with advanced technology and agricultural methods.What We OfferWe provide a supportive and collaborative work environment with opportunities for professional development and growth. Here, you'll be part of a company that values quality and sustainability, while working in a dynamic environment where your efforts make a difference.About the JobAs an agronomist, you will plan and lead cultivation work in our greenhouse. Your primary responsibilities will include:Monitoring and adjusting climate and irrigation systems to ensure optimal plant growth.Conducting daily plant health checks and managing pest control in collaboration with the IPM Manager.Coordinating and assigning tasks to your team, including two junior agronomists.Documenting and reporting data on climate, irrigation, and cultivation processes, as well as proposing improvements.Ensuring compliance with hygiene, safety, and food standards.You will also serve as a backup for the Chief Agronomist when needed and work closely with other teams to ensure smooth and efficient operations.About YouWe are looking for someone who has:A degree in agronomy or equivalent experience.Previous experience in greenhouse cultivation, preferably high-wire tomato production.Knowledge of climate systems such as Priva or Hoogendoorn is a strong advantage.Excellent leadership skills and the ability to motivate and develop team members.Strong communication skills in both Swedish and English.Additionally, you are detail-oriented, flexible, and resilient under pressure, with a strong focus on teamwork and problem-solving.Recruitment Within the EUWe welcome candidates from across the EU to apply for this position. However, to qualify as a candidate, you must have a valid work permit to work in Sweden.How to ApplyIf you're ready to take the next step in your career and become part of our successful team, send your CV and a cover letter to Linda@frovigreenery.se. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Last day to apply is on 28 of March 2025.
j.id: 1836155", "j.title: Produktionsledare/Driftledare med inriktning dikor och växtodling Svartsjö
j.description: The correctional service is growing - we are building new, rebuilding and building more and are now looking for more employees. Our most important goal is to reduce recidivism - to break the vicious cycle. If we succeed in that, society will be safer and more secure for everyone. We are the authority responsible for prisons, probation, custody and client transport. Do you want to know more? Hear what our employees think about working within the Correctional Service: https://www.kriminalvarden.se/jobba-hos-oss/We are now looking for a new colleague for Svartsjö agriculture, which belongs to the Stockholm West business area, located in Ekerö municipality. It is possible to get to work via both the south and west side of Stockholm. About 170 employees and ten managers manage, lead and develop the business, which receives approx. 270 inmates. Agriculture is part of the clients' daily occupation during its execution. The farm covers 400 hectares, of which 310 hectares are arable land and 90 hectares are pasture. Farming includes 250 hectares of grain and 60 hectares of paddy, as well as fodder crops such as wheat, oats, peas, broad beans and canola.  The farm has a breeding herd of the Hereford breed. We get around 75 calves per season and have around 160 animals in total. The machinery park is modern with GPS technology and a workshop for service. The business also includes firewood production, vegetable growing, green area maintenance and carpentry. There are well-equipped staff areas with gyms and charging stations. JOB DUTIES As a production manager/operations manager, you get a central and inspiring role where you are primarily responsible for the animals together with three colleagues. During the crop growing season, you broaden your role and collaborate with the team on the crop growing side, which includes more other colleagues. The daily work is carried out by the institution's inmates, and you become an important role model who, with your commitment, motivates and guides them in their working life. You will have a workforce of approx. 10-15 clients depending on the season. Here you have the chance to influence and make a difference to contribute to the Correctional Service's vision Better out. The role is both diverse and eventful, and it requires good basic physics because the tasks are often physically demanding. Here you get the opportunity to work hands-on and develop together with committed colleagues all while making a real difference. Working as a production manager means that you contribute to a better society. In order to enjoy and succeed in your assignment, it is important that you share the Prison Service's basic values ​​of a humane view of people, respect for the individual and the belief that people can be developed. has practical experience and a strong interest in work management in animal husbandry and crop cultivation. As a production manager, you have clear and pedagogical insight into how best to introduce and supervise inmates from the institution, while actively participating in the tasks yourself. You are also welcome to apply for the position if you are only interested in working with the animals. We have the opportunity to send staff on training courses that are relevant to being able to cope with the tasks, in addition to this, we have a solid individual introduction. We attach great importance to personal suitability. We are looking for you who have: • High school education or other education, preferably in nature management, agriculture and animal care in combination with work experience • Good knowledge of the Swedish language both spoken and written • B driving license It is advantageous if you have :• Work experience from a managerial role, preferably operations manager, barn foreman or farm manager• Experience as an animal keeper with experience from a cattle and/or dairy herd or other animal husbandry in agriculture and equine farming• Knowledge in semining• Experience with cattle, including practical calving experience• Experience in crop cultivation• Forklift license or other driver's license such as wheel loader, clearing saw, chainsaw OTHERWe place high demands on our employees' security and privacy awareness. To work with us, you need to undergo a security assessment in accordance with the Security Protection Act. For this position, a security screening interview will be conducted before a decision on employment is made. During the security check, you as a person, your background and your relationships are investigated from a security perspective. In connection with your employment interview, you will receive more information about security clearance. Read more about the security check at: https://www.kriminalvarden.se/jobba-hos-oss/rekryteringsprocessen/sakerhetsprovning-vid-rekrytering/Kriminalvården strives for an even gender distribution and increased diversity. Probationary employment may be applied. To submit your application, click on the application link in the advertisement. Ask questions about how to apply and submit your CV directly to Visma Recruit. Questions about specific jobs are answered by the contact person specified in the advertisement. We kindly but firmly refrain from direct contact with staffing and recruitment companies and sellers of recruitment advertisements. The Correctional Service has procured contracts.
